title: 机器人跑半马与章鱼的梦
pdf: https://michael-podcast-1513696684.cos.ap-chengdu.myqcloud.com/vol11/Vol11_晚读讲义_机器人跑半马与章鱼的梦_v1.pdf

blocks.en: Hello, explorers, and welcome back to Michael's Morning Listening! This is our eleventh show together — keep going for a fortnight, and we'll hit twenty! Today we meet a runner with legs of metal in Beijing. Then we dive under the sea, to watch an octopus paint dreams on its skin. No flying saucers today — but there will be running and dreams. Ready? Let's go!
blocks.title: 开场白
blocks.cn: 你好，探险家们，欢迎回到 Michael 的早听晚读！这是我们在一起的第十一期节目——再坚持两周，我们就到二十期啦！今天我们先认识一位在北京跑步的金属腿选手；然后潜入海底，看一只章鱼把梦画在自己的皮肤上。今天没有飞碟——但会有奔跑，会有美梦。准备好了吗？出发！

blocks.en: On your marks, get set... go! In Beijing, twenty-one humanoid robots lined up for a race: the world's first half-marathon for robots — twenty-one kilometres beside thousands of human runners. The robots came in all sizes: some no taller than a small child, others as tall as a basketball player. Thousands of fans came to observe. One robot wore running shoes. One wore boxing gloves! One robot fell on its face, waved its arms, and got up again.
blocks.title: 机器人跑半程马拉松
blocks.cn: 各就各位，预备……跑！在北京，二十一个机器人排成一排，参加一场比赛：世界上第一场机器人半程马拉松——二十一公里的路，旁边是几千名人类跑者。这些机器人个头各异：有的还没小朋友高，有的像篮球运动员一样高。几千名观众赶来围观。一台机器人穿着跑鞋，一台戴着拳击手套！还有一台机器人脸朝下摔了一跤，它挥挥胳膊，又爬了起来。

blocks.en: The winner was a tall robot called Tiangong Ultra: one point eight metres of metal and wires, fifty-five kilograms. It crossed the finish line in two hours, forty minutes and forty-two seconds, stopping only three times for a new battery. The fastest human needed one hour and two minutes — so the robots have homework to do! Building a running robot means compromise: long legs run fast, but they drink power. The engineers were determined anyway. Why race? Not for medals, and not for justice — every robot that finished was a hero. When Tiangong Ultra crossed the line, the crowd erupted with cheers.
blocks.title: 机器人跑半程马拉松
blocks.cn: 冠军是一台高大的机器人，叫“天工Ultra”：一米八的金属和电线，重五十五公斤。它用两小时四十分四十二秒冲过终点线，中途只停了三次换新电池。最快的人类跑者只用了一小时零两分钟——所以机器人还有“家庭作业”要做呢！造一台会跑步的机器人，处处都要折中：腿长跑得快，可腿长也费电。不过工程师们还是下定了决心。为什么要比赛呢？不是为了奖牌，也不是为了争输赢——每一台跑到终点的机器人都是英雄。当天工Ultra冲过终点线时，人群爆发出一阵欢呼。

blocks.en: Now, from the noisy road to a quiet sea. In Japan, scientists watched twenty-nine sleeping octopuses — and found a surprise. An octopus sleeps in two ways. In quiet sleep, it lies pale and still, like a stone. But about once an hour, it slips into active sleep for one minute — and the show begins! Its skin flashes red, brown and gold. Its eyes roll. Its eight arms, like the branches of a tree, twitch and wave as it breathes faster. Under the skin sit tiny colour cells called chromatophores, turning the colours up and down like a dial.
blocks.title: 会做梦的章鱼
blocks.cn: 现在，从热闹的马路来到安静的大海。在日本，科学家观察了二十九只正在睡觉的章鱼——发现了一个惊喜。章鱼有两种睡眠。在安静睡眠时，它趴着不动，皮肤苍白，像一块石头。但大约每隔一小时，它会滑进活跃睡眠，持续一分钟——表演开始了！它的皮肤闪烁着红色、棕色和金色，眼睛转动，八条像树枝一样的胳膊轻轻抽动、挥舞，呼吸也变快了。皮肤下面藏着微小的色素细胞，能像拧表盘一样把颜色调亮、调暗。

blocks.en: Stranger still, its brain buzzes with the patterns it uses when awake and hiding — or hunting. So scientists think the octopus may be replaying its day: it may be dreaming! When the team kept the octopuses awake too long, they fell into active sleep sooner, and more often — like you after a busy day. And after a meal, an octopus rests to digest its food... and perhaps to dream about it. The team hopes this helps conservation: the better we understand sea animals, the better we can protect their homes.
blocks.title: 会做梦的章鱼
blocks.cn: 更奇怪的是，它睡觉时的大脑会活跃地“嗡嗡”作响，发出和它清醒时一样的忙碌信号——那正是它躲藏或者捕猎时用的信号。所以科学家认为，章鱼可能在重播白天发生的事：它可能在做梦！当研究人员让章鱼太久不睡觉时，它们会更快、更频繁地进入活跃睡眠——就像你忙了一整天之后那样。吃完饭后，章鱼会休息一下，消化食物……说不定，还顺便梦一梦那顿饭。研究团队希望，这项工作也能帮助保护海洋：我们越了解海里的动物，就越能保护好它们的家。

blocks.en: Here's today's idiom: 'break the ice.' Long ago, ships broke the ice on frozen rivers so other boats could pass. Today, when strangers meet, things can feel cold and quiet — until someone tells a joke or asks a question. That breaks the ice! Example: 'At my new school, I broke the ice by sharing my sandwiches.' Who will you break the ice with this week?
blocks.title: 今日俚语
blocks.cn: 今天的俚语是“break the ice”（打破僵局）：很久以前，坚固的船会破开冻河上的冰，让别的船通过。今天，陌生人刚见面时，气氛可能又冷又安静——直到有人讲个笑话，或者问一个问题。那就把“冰”打破啦！举个例子：“在新学校，我靠分享我的三明治打破了僵局。”这一周，你想和谁打破僵局呢？

blocks.en: Let's think about the stories. A robot ran a half-marathon, and an octopus dreamed in colours. Two questions for you. First: is a robot race relevant to your life? The legs that run today may carry bags and help grandparents tomorrow — would you like to race a robot? Second: tonight, watch your cat on the kitchen floor. Do you think it dreams, like the octopus? Talk with your family!
blocks.title: 结束语与互动问题
blocks.cn: 我们来想想今天的故事。一台机器人跑完了半程马拉松，一只章鱼在梦里闪烁着颜色。现在有两个问题。第一：机器人比赛和你的生活相关吗？今天奔跑的腿，将来可能帮我们提重物、照顾爷爷奶奶——你想和机器人赛跑吗？第二：今晚，看看你家睡在厨房地板上的猫。你觉得它会像章鱼一样做梦吗？和家人聊一聊吧！

blocks.en: That's all for today, explorers. Run like the robot, dream like the octopus, and break the ice wherever you go. See you tomorrow morning!
blocks.title: 告别
blocks.cn: 今天的节目就到这里啦，探险家们。像机器人一样奔跑，像章鱼一样做梦，到哪里都去打破坚冰。明天早上见！

quiz.title: B. 单项选择（Single Choice）
questions:
How long was the robot race in Beijing?
A. Five kilometres
B. Twenty-one kilometres
C. Forty-two kilometres
D. One hundred kilometres

What did Tiangong Ultra do three times during the race?
A. Fall on its face
B. Wave to the fans
C. Stop for a new battery
D. Sing a song

In active sleep, what does the octopus's skin do?
A. Turns hard like a shell
B. Flashes red, brown and gold
C. Falls off
D. Grows longer arms

What does "break the ice" mean?
A. Help new people feel friendly and start talking
B. Smash the ice on a river
C. Win a running race
D. Sleep for a long time

children.text: Its eight arms twitch and wave.
（它的八条胳膊轻轻抽动、挥舞）主语
连接——这是英语里“一个主语做两个动作”的标准写法。
like the branches of a tree
＝“像……一样”，把八条胳膊比作树枝。两个逗号把它和主干隔开——读到这里可以先跳过它，读完主干再回头看比喻，句子一下就通了。
”：胳膊抽动挥舞，和呼吸变快是
的。注意这不是原因，只是“同一时间”。
胳膊抽动又挥舞（主干）→ 像树枝一样（like 插入比喻，描样子）→ 同时它呼吸变快了（as 补出同时发生的另一件事）
。一句话同时拍下了章鱼活跃睡眠里三个一起出现的动作。

"crossed the finish line in two hours, forty minutes and forty-two seconds, stopping only three times for a new battery."
"its skin flashes red, brown and gold. Its eyes roll."

words.clue: A very long running race — our robots ran a half one, twenty-one kilometres.
Pictures your brain shows you while you sleep; the octopus may have them too.
It stores power; the winning robot stopped three times for a fresh one.
A period of two weeks: 'Keep going for a ____, and we'll hit twenty!'
The round face of a clock; the octopus turns its colours up and down like one.
To watch something carefully — thousands of fans came to do this at the race.
People once thought they saw flying ones in the sky. 'No flying ____ today!'
A sea animal with eight arms that can change the colour of its skin.
A middle way between two wants: long legs run fast, but they drink power.
To burst out suddenly — the crowd did this with cheers at the finish line.
